title: [objectql] TRUE readonlyWhen strips beforeUpdate-derived values too — a conditionally-locked derived field has no server-side write path at all (isSystem included), unlike static readonly's hook-stamp protection
body:
## Summary

On the by-id UPDATE path, `stripReadonlyWhenFields` runs **after** the `beforeUpdate` hooks, is keyed on `name in data` over the **post-hook** payload, and is **not** gated on `opCtx.context?.isSystem`. The static `readonly` strip immediately below it has both protections: it is skipped entirely for `isSystem` callers, and its `suppliedValues` discipline drops only caller-forged writes — the code comment states the intent verbatim: *"suppliedValues ensures only caller-forged read-only writes are dropped, never the server stamps — and (#5591) never a stamp a hook wrote OVER a key the caller happened to echo back."*

Consequence: a field locked by a TRUE `readonlyWhen` predicate has **no write path at all** for server-derived values. A `beforeUpdate` hook computes it — stripped. A cron/plugin writes it with `{ context: { isSystem: true } }` — stripped. The engine's own strict-mode refusal text documents the behavior (*"this exempts statically 'readonly' fields, but NOT fields locked by a TRUE 'readonlyWhen' predicate — those stay locked for every caller"*), so the "every caller" half may well be deliberate — but it never got the derived-write story static `readonly` got: the strip that exists to stop **caller forgeries** also silently discards **server-authored stamps**, and no sanctioned alternative channel exists.

Net effect: **the derived-field pattern (hook-computed column) and conditional readonly cannot coexist on one field.** An author who wants "visible on the form but locked" (which `hidden` cannot give, and static `readonly` historically did not render at all in that project's form) plus "recomputed by a hook" has no spec-compliant spelling.

## Where (origin/main @ bb3def43c254)

- [`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` L9528](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/bb3def43c254/packages/objectql/src/engine.ts#L9528): `stripReadonlyWhenFields(...)` — unconditional, runs on `hookContext.input.data` after the before-phase hooks (ADR-0058 Addendum II ordering).
- [`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` L9556](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/bb3def43c254/packages/objectql/src/engine.ts#L9556): `stripReadonlyFields(...)` — inside `if (!opCtx.context?.isSystem)`, with `suppliedValues`, so hook stamps survive (#5591 comment directly above).
- [`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/bb3def43c254/packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts) `stripReadonlyWhenFields`: `if (!def?.readonlyWhen || !(name in data)) continue;` — `data` is the post-hook payload, so a key a hook added is judged exactly like a key the caller sent.
- [`packages/objectql/src/readonly-strict-errors.ts`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/bb3def43c254/packages/objectql/src/readonly-strict-errors.ts): the strict-mode refusal text quoted above.

The multi-row branch (L9697/L9710) has the same shape.

## Minimal repro

Standalone — one object, one hook, no app dependency:

```ts
// demo.object.ts — a derived date that must stay form-visible but user-locked
fields: {
  period_days: { type: 'number' },
  next_date:   { type: 'date', readonlyWhen: P`true` },
}

// demo hook
beforeUpdate: (ctx) => {
  // derive next_date from the payload / prior record
  ctx.input.data.next_date = addDays(today, ctx.input.data.period_days ?? 90);
}

// caller — system context, by-id update
await engine.update('demo', id, { period_days: 90 }, { context: { isSystem: true } });
```

Observed on `@objectstack/objectql` 17.0.0: `period_days` lands; the hook-computed `next_date` is stripped with reason `readonly_when` (visible via `options.onFieldsDropped`; with `strictReadonlyWrites` the refusal message is the one quoted above). The row keeps the stale value. Same outcome for a plain user-context PATCH, a plugin/cron write without context, and `{ context: { isSystem: true } }` — there is no caller for which the hook's value persists.

## Expected — one of (decision needed, ascending cost)

- **A. `suppliedValues` parity (recommended).** Give `stripReadonlyWhenFields` the same key discipline #5591 gave the static strip: judge only engine-entry caller-supplied keys, never keys a hook added or overwrote. The caller-facing lock is unchanged — a client cannot turn its own key into a "hook-written" one — and the mechanism and its rationale are already accepted in this file. "Locked for every caller" stays true at the API boundary; it stops being true only for the server's own trusted hooks, which is exactly the static-readonly status quo pinned in #4903.
- **B. `isSystem` parity.** Honor `{ context: { isSystem: true } }` for `readonlyWhen` like static readonly. Weaker: it flips the documented "every caller" wording, and it lets *any* system-context write bypass a state lock (the paid-invoice-frozen-lines case #4889 is built on) — probably not what a state lock means.
- **C. An official derived-field write channel.** Keep the strip total and add sanctioned vocabulary (a field-level "derived by hook" declaration, or an engine option scoped narrower than `isSystem`). Cleanest contract, biggest surface.

If instead "total lock, hooks included" is confirmed as the intended contract, it should be (a) stated in the spec/docs for `readonlyWhen` — today only the strict-mode error text says it — and (b) lint-visible: an object whose own hook assigns a field that also declares a `readonlyWhen` that is TRUE in that state is authoring a write that can never land. That is a declared-vs-enforced gap a publish-time gate could reject loudly instead of letting it fail as a silent runtime strip.

## Real-world impact (measured, downstream)

Part of steedos-labs/os-project-titanwind-ehr#1446. `equipment.next_maintenance_date` is hook-derived (last maintenance date + cycle days) and was declared with an always-true `readonlyWhen` to render visible-but-locked on the edit form. After a maintenance sign-off the recompute silently never landed (HTTP 200, field dropped), and a scheduler keyed on that date regenerated the same maintenance plan on every scan — a user-visible duplicate-plans loop, diagnosed only by reading the engine's strip order in the dist bundle.

The app shipped a metadata-level workaround (steedos-labs/os-project-titanwind-ehr#1451): the predicate became `!has(record.maint_recalc) || record.maint_recalc != true`, plus a hidden always-locked boolean token field the hook sets in the same payload — the token itself is always stripped (never persists), but the merged-snapshot evaluation (`readonlyWhenBindings`, `{ ...previous, ...data }`) reads it within that one update, so the derived value survives. It stays inside declared platform semantics — no driver bypass, no node_modules patch — and the project is **not blocked**. But it is exactly the kind of clever in-band pattern AI-authored metadata will now copy everywhere a derived field needs a form lock. We would retire it for an official channel; recording that unblock condition here.

## Versions

`@objectstack/objectql` 17.0.0 (npm `latest` at filing time). Behavior reproduced on 17.0.0 GA; strip ordering and gating verified unchanged on `origin/main` @ bb3def43c254.

Prior-art sweep before filing: #3042 / #3044 (multi-row enforcement), #4889 / #4972 (parent scope), #4953 / #6454 (total-record materialization), #4903 (static readonly vs plugin-write asymmetry — closed with the hook-stamp mechanism documented and the asymmetry pinned), #6437 (`DroppedFieldsEvent.reason`), #3425 (static `readonly` semantics formalized). None covers the hook-derived / `isSystem` gap for `readonlyWhen`.
